title: Tommy Ramone on why Johnny Ramone's playing forced him to switch from managing to drumming (Janelle Borg, Guitar World, 24 April 2024)
notes: Quotes an interview with Tommy Ramone: "When we were trying out drummers none of them worked out because their drumming just didn't click in with Johnny's guitar style"; "Most people were playing like John Bonham or Carmine Appice; they were incredible drummers, but their use of tom-toms and rolls just didn't fit with what the Ramones were doing"; "I wanted to lock in with the guitar and try and get a forward momentum going"; "I locked in with Johnny, and Dee Dee's bass was the underpinning of it all. Johnny had this very flowing thing because of his strumming technique." The debut "a lo-fi work of art".

title: Last Ramones Standing (John Piccarella, The Village Voice, 12 October 2004)
notes: Tommy and Marky Ramone interviewed together. Marky: "the eighth-note high hat playing and the cymbal and floor tom playing created a wall of sound, and it was a challenge"; he learned Tommy's parts from tapes of the records and the live show. Tommy, on taking over from Joey Ramone on drums: "With Joey it was a very choppy sound, sort of like a jagged rockabilly ... the major change was smoothing it out, giving it a flowing feel, more of a propulsive kind of straight-ahead feel. John's guitar playing and the drumming I was doing really did click." "The speed is pure Johnny."

title: Here's the Ramones' 1975 Band Bio, Written by Tommy Ramone (Colin Joyce, Spin, 12 July 2014)
notes: The 1975 press biography Tommy wrote: "Tommy is the drummer whose pulsating playing launches the throbbing sound of the band"; "Their sound is not unlike a fast drill on a rear molar."

title: Tommy Ramone (interview, READ Magazine, 30 November 1998; ReadJunk)
notes: "As far as the drumming is concerned, I became the drummer because I couldn't explain to drummers what they needed. They just couldn't get it or understand it, so I started doing it."
